s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic autoimmune disorder with sicca symptoms, Raynaud phenomenon, and calcinosis
salient_findings: 20-year history of oral and ocular sicca symptoms
Asymptomatic elevation of creatinine kinase levels
Chronic stable autoimmune thrombocytopenia
Painless pinpoint white nodules in the subcutaneous plane of the right fifth finger
Soft-tissue calcifications in the distal first and fifth fingers
key_facts: 56-year-old woman
History of hypothyroidism and hyperlipidemia
20-year history of oral and ocular sicca symptoms
Asymptomatic elevation of creatinine kinase levels
Negative myositis and muscular dystrophy panel
Negative muscle biopsy results
Chronic stable autoimmune thrombocytopenia
Previous medications included methotrexate and low-dose steroids
Currently on hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily
Does not take calcium or vitamin D supplements
Mild dryness of mouth and throat
Raynaud phenomenon
Painless pinpoint white nodules in the subcutaneous plane of the right fifth finger
Soft-tissue calcifications in the distal first and fifth fingers
Positive for antinuclear antibody 1:160 titer, nucleolar pattern, and anti-Ro
Biopsy of digit lesions from right thumb and fourth finger consistent with calcinosis

shortlist.label: Limited systemic scleroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has Raynaud phenomenon, calcinosis, and positive antinuclear antibody, which are characteristic features of limited systemic scleroderma

shortlist.label: Sjögren's syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has 20-year history of oral and ocular sicca symptoms, which is a hallmark of Sjögren's syndrome

shortlist.label: Mixed connective tissue disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has overlapping features of different autoimmune diseases, including sicca symptoms, Raynaud phenomenon, and positive antinuclear antibody

shortlist.label: Calcinosis cutis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has biopsy-proven calcinosis and soft-tissue calcifications in the distal fingers

shortlist.label: CREST syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has Calcinosis, Raynaud phenomenon, Esophageal dysmotility is not mentioned but has sicca symptoms, and Telangiectasia is not mentioned, but has a positive antinuclear antibody

raw.rationale: Patient's symptoms and test results, including Raynaud phenomenon, soft-tissue calcifications, and positive anti-Ro antibody, are consistent with CREST syndrome, a subtype of limited systemic scleroderma.

rejected.label: Sjögren's syndrome
rejected.why: While patient has sicca symptoms, other findings such as calcinosis and Raynaud phenomenon are more specific to CREST syndrome.

rejected.label: Mixed connective tissue disease
rejected.why: Patient's symptoms and test results do not meet the full criteria for mixed connective tissue disease.

rejected.label: Calcinosis cutis
rejected.why: Calcinosis cutis is a symptom, not a disease, and patient's other symptoms are more consistent with CREST syndrome.

rejected.label: Limited systemic scleroderma
rejected.why: CREST syndrome is a subtype of limited systemic scleroderma and better explains patient's specific symptoms and test results.
